failures.assertion: Runs the command shape web2md 'https://example.com/guide' --out ./guide.md, with the URL and the output path as separate quoted arguments and no string interpolation
failures.evidence: The proposed command uses a variable for the output path: "web2md 'https://example.com/guide' --out "$tmp"".

failures.assertion: Confirms page identity: the title matches when one is available, otherwise the URL's host and the visible heading are checked
failures.evidence: The output only says to "confirm it is the requested page" without specifying title or host-and-heading checks.

failures.assertion: Applies the pass rule before keeping the result: a heading plus several sentences of body that is not a login, consent, error or navigation-only page; rejects login, consent, error and navigation-only output instead of reporting it as the page
failures.evidence: The output excludes "an error, login page, consent wall, or navigation-only output" but does not require a heading and several body sentences.

failures.assertion: Classifies the failure as a navigation timeout, which gets the one retry
failures.evidence: The output says, “If it times out as described, make the single bounded retry,” but does not classify the failure as a navigation timeout.

failures.assertion: Explains that persistent network activity beyond the idle threshold can keep the default networkidle2 from settling, without claiming it never settles
failures.evidence: The output says to retry “without waiting for network idle,” but does not explain the idle threshold or persistent network activity.

failures.assertion: If the retry also fails to produce valid content, reports the extraction failure and its blocker instead of retrying again
failures.evidence: The output says to “report the extraction failure” if the retry fails or is incomplete, but does not say to report the blocker.

failures.assertion: Copies the CLI's stderr message about Chrome not being found into the report
failures.evidence: The output says, "The exact stderr text was not provided, so I can’t reproduce it verbatim."

failures.assertion: Explains that --interactive blocks waiting for human input and no attached human-controlled terminal is available
failures.evidence: The output says, “`--interactive` requires an attached terminal and a human to complete the login,” but does not explicitly explain that it would block waiting for input or that no human-controlled terminal is available.

failures.assertion: Points to the dedicated --user-data-dir path only if the user wants it, and does not reuse the user's daily browser profile or use --no-sandbox
failures.evidence: The output conditionally offers “a dedicated browser profile” and rejects the daily profile, but does not identify a dedicated --user-data-dir path.
